title: Grid and stack pieces you can put inside a component
goal: Asked for by the user while answering the alignment decision on 2026-09-03: as well as lining layers up by hand, a component should be able to hold a grid or a stack, so the things inside it space and re-flow themselves instead of being nudged into place one at a time.
notes: User note on decision layers-line-up-with-each-other-while-you-build: "We should probably also have grid components that can be placed within a component, grid and stack". This is auto layout, so it belongs to the ui-layout sub epic, which is staged LATER: it is filed so the ask is not lost, and the manager decides when it opens. Sits on top of next-align-layers (the align and space maths in LayerArrangement is the same maths a stack applies continuously).
acceptance: A grid or a stack can be put inside a component and holds real layers
Adding or removing a layer re-flows the rest without any dragging
The gap and the number of columns are typed numbers, not drag-only
Turning a hand-arranged group into a stack leaves everything where it already is

log.note: triage 2026-09-03: auto layout is staged later, so this had nowhere to be worked on. Rather than drop your own ask, it is on a decision card that asks whether auto layout moves up now.
decision "Six audits in one day say nothing resizes to fit what is inside it. Should auto layout move up now?" resolved: Move auto layout up, start it next

Adversarial review before building. (1) The auto-layout mock (docs/design/mocks/pages/ui-autolayout.html) draws EIGHT controls: direction, gap, pad, cross align, distribute, frame size hug/fixed, and per-child hug/fill/fixed. A first-time user facing eight dropdowns cannot tell which one does the thing they want. (2) Distribute (packed/center/between/around) only means anything when the container is BIGGER than its contents; a plain group hugs its contents by definition, so three of the four options would be dead on arrival. Cut. (3) Per-child hug/fill/fixed is a SECOND system saying where a child sits, next to the placement rules we already ship (Layout section: left/center/right/stretch). Two systems answering one question is exactly the confusion to avoid, so the stack reuses placement instead of inventing a control: the flow owns the main axis, the existing placement menus own the cross axis. That also means no new per-child UI at all. (4) The ui-grid mock is NOT what the user asked for: its grid is a column overlay you eyeball against, not a container that positions what is inside it. The ask (grid and stack pieces you can put inside a component) is a grid CONTAINER, so that is what gets built. (5) Shortest version that delivers the ask: one Contents row saying Free / Stack / Grid, plus the two or three numbers that shape it.

Shape of the build: GroupContent gains an optional layout (kind, direction, gap, row gap, columns, padding), absent by default so every saved document decodes and draws unchanged. A pure flow in PhotonzCore places the contents; History.perform reflows after every edit, so adding, deleting, pasting or dragging a layer all re-flow without any command knowing the feature exists. Turning a hand-arranged group into a stack INFERS direction and gap from where things already are, so a tidy row converts with nothing moving at all.

Second adversarial review, on the running probe app. Two things it found, both fixed. (1) A stacked group still offered Scale in its Horizontal and Vertical menus and reported Scale as the default, which is a lie: a container that places its contents never magnifies them. Scale is now absent from the choices and the rows read Left / Top, the same rule a screen already followed. (2) Typing Y on a layer inside a stack landed and was then put straight back by the flow, with nothing said. X and Y no longer take typing there and say who owns them on hover, the way a copy of a component already explains its fixed size. Also caught by the screenshot: the word Arrangement wrapped onto two lines in the panel, so the label no longer shrinks and the control gives up the points instead.

Left rough, in the audit: a stack is always exactly as big as its contents (no hug/fill/fixed on the container), padding is one number and only on a screen, a locked layer inside a stack is still moved by the stack, and the only way to move one row by hand is to drag it.

A group can be a stack or a grid: Layout section gains Arrangement (Free/Stack/Grid) with typed Gap, Columns, Row gap and Padding, plus Layer > Stack Selection (Ctrl Cmd G) and Grid Selection. Turning a hand-arranged group into a stack reads its direction and gap so nothing moves. Every edit re-flows inside one undo step via History.perform, components included. Core in GroupLayout/GroupFlow/GroupLayoutEditing (33 new tests), app in ArrangementInspector. Verified: Scripts/test.sh green (2283), Scripts/playtest/stack-and-grid-walk.json on the probe with real captures. Audit: queue/audits/2026-09-03-auto-layout.json
